changelog: 1.0.0 — première version : usage québécois (OQLF), glossaire des termes choisis, passages douteux signalés ; pas une traduction certifiée.

inputs.prompt: Turn this English site or product copy into French-first copy that keeps the brand voice: {{inputs.englishCopy}}. Brand voice: {{inputs.brandVoice}}. Firm glossary: {{inputs.glossary}}. French must be at least as prominent as the English: write the French first, then keep the English equivalent right after each block. Not a word-for-word translation: Québec usage, natural phrasing. The first line of your answer is exactly this sentence: fr « Traduction automatisée non certifiée — à faire réviser par un professionnel avant tout usage, surtout pour un document juridique. » en « Automated, uncertified translation — to be reviewed by a professional before any use, above all for a legal document. » (use the one that matches the output language). Mark anything you are unsure of as « À réviser » (fr) or « To review » (en). Name the terminology source of every term you choose (the usage recommended by the Office québécois de la langue française, OQLF, and its Grand dictionnaire terminologique, when one applies; otherwise say « usage courant »). Never invent a legal term: when no established Québec term exists, keep the source term in brackets and flag the passage. Never quote a statute; refer to it by name only.
